Clara Raises $105 Million to Grow Latin American Corporate Spend Management Platform
By Julie Muhn (@julieschicktanz) Posted on November 13, 2026
Categories: Daily news , Funding
Clara raised $105 million, comprising a $65 million Series C equity round and the renewal of a $40 million growth financing facility, bringing its total debt and equity funding to $838 million.
Clara will use the funding to expand its market reach and enhance its AI capabilities, including its MCP integration that enables AI agents to access financial data and execute authorized transactions.
The funding comes amid global growth in corporate card and spend management platforms, as providers expand beyond payments and expense tracking to offer integrated, AI-powered financial management tools.
Brazil-based spend management platform Clara raised $105 million this week. The round is comprised of $65 million in equity in a Series C round and the renewal of a $40 million growth financing facility from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF).
The $65 million Series C was anchored by Citius, Kaszek, and DEG, a subsidiary of Germany’s KfW Group. The round also attracted participation from 10 existing investors and three new investors, including CMT Digital and Nascent VC.
The latest investment brings Clara’s total debt and equity funding to $838 million, following several debt financing deals over the past year. In November 2025, Clara secured $70 million in structured debt financing from BBVA Spark, Covalto, and the International Finance Corporation (IFC). Three months later, the company renewed a $150 million credit facility with Goldman Sachs, bringing its total debt capacity to more than $250 million.
Clara will use today’s funding to expand its go-to-market team and strengthen the automation and AI capabilities of its platform. Clara was founded in 2020 and now helps more than 45,000 businesses automate routine work, control spending, and make better financial decisions. The company’s platform offers corporate cards, bill payments, spend management, accounts payable, and accounts receivable to help businesses make and manage payments. Along with the financing announcement, Clara said it has also surpassed $100 million in annualized net revenue and maintained positive EBITDA for more than a year.
Among Clara’s capabilities is its Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration, which connects the platform with AI agents to enable customers to access real-time spending reports and forecasts using natural language, as well as execute authorized transactions autonomously. The company also offers AI-powered policy enforcement that checks employee expenses against company policies in real time, global spend management tools that allow businesses to manage expenses across countries and currencies, and fleet management solutions that support fuel payments and vehicle operations.
“Clara exists to champion Latin American businesses, and we work tirelessly to give them the tools to compete and win on the global stage,” said Clara Co-Founder and CEO Gerry Giacomán Colyer. “The region has long been underserved by financial platforms designed for other markets. We’re combining AI with local expertise to solve challenges specific to doing business here and give our customers a distinct competitive edge.”

articles.title: Addex Spin-out Neurosterix Closes $105 Million Series B Financing
articles.snippet: Addex Spin-out Neurosterix Closes $105 Million Series B Financing GlobeNewswire
articles.text:
Ad Hoc Announcement Pursuant to Art. 53 LR
Geneva, Switzerland, November 11, 2026 - Addex Therapeutics (SIX and Nasdaq: ADXN), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a portfolio of novel small molecule allosteric modulators for neurological disorders, today announced that its spin-out company, Neurosterix, has closed a $105 million Series B financing from a syndicate of leading life science investors. Addex did not participate in the financing and its equity interest now represents 8.5% of the issued capital at a valuation of $18.6 million.
The proceeds raised will support mainly the planned Phase 2 clinical development of NTX-253, a highly selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulator (PAM), for schizophrenia. The financing will also support Neurosterix’s broader pipeline of selective allosteric modulators for a range of neuropsychiatric disorders.
“The closing of this significant financing is a huge endorsement of the allosteric approach pioneered by Addex in schizophrenia as well as other neuropsychiatric disorders. Congatulations to the whole Neurosterix team, which has made enormous strides in advancing lead program NTX-253 through clinical development and ready for Phase 2, following our spin-out in 2024,” said Tim Dyer, CEO of Addex.
About NTX-253 and M4 PAMs
The M4 muscarinic receptor is a validated target for treating schizophrenia and related disorders through indirect modulation of dopamine signaling. NTX-253 is a potent, highly selective, oral PAM of M4 that fine-tunes muscarinic signaling in the brain to potentially reduce psychosis symptoms while avoiding the movement disorders and metabolic complications associated with traditional dopamine antagonists. Neurosterix has completed Phase 1 single- and multiple-ascending-dose clinical studies of NTX-253, which data supporting advancing into larger scale Phase 2 clinical studies.
About Neurosterix
Neurosterix is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on transforming neuropsychiatric care through selective allosteric modulation. The company’s approach is designed to fine-tune brain signaling with greater precision and selectivity, with the goal of developing safer, more effective treatments for people living with schizophrenia, and mood and anxiety disorders. Neurosterix’s pipeline includes NTX-253, a selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulator (PAM) for schizophrenia; NTX-819, a potentially first-in-class mGlu7 negative allosteric modulator (NAM) for mood and anxiety disorders; and NTX-529, a second differentiated M4 PAM for additional psychosis- and mood-related disorders. Neurosterix has operations in Boston and Geneva. For more information, visit www.neurosterix.com.
About Addex Therapeutics
Addex Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a portfolio of novel small molecule allosteric modulators for neurological disorders. Addex's lead drug candidate, dipraglurant (mGlu5 negative allosteric modulator or NAM), is under evaluation for future development in brain injury recovery, including post-stroke and traumatic brain injury recovery. Addex has selected a GABAB PAM drug candidate for development in substance use disorders and has successfully completed IND enabling studies. In addition, Addex is advancing a differentiated GABAB PAM compound for the treatment of chronic cough. Jupiter Medical Center Foundation Raises Record $102 Million in Single Fiscal Year
Posted by cfelixcpa | Nov 15, 2026 | SF STAT! | 0 |
Fundraising milestone puts independent not-for-profit on par with academic health systems
November 3, 2026 – Jupiter Medical Center Foundation raised more than $102 million in philanthropic support during fiscal year 2026, marking the largest fundraising year in its history and a milestone aligned with much larger academic and multi-hospital health systems. The Foundation’s record-breaking success reflects a 61% increase in giving over the past three years.
More than 2,300 donors contributed between October 1, 2025, and September 30, 2026, fueling the continued transformation of Jupiter Medical Center (JMC), the region’s only independent, not-for-profit health system, anchored by a 340-bed hospital. Their support is accelerating investments in physician recruitment, advanced technology, expanded specialty services, research and future facilities designed to meet the growing healthcare needs of Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast.
“This milestone reflects a historic and transformative year for the future of healthcare for the region,” said Amit Rastogi, MD, MHCM, President and CEO of Jupiter Medical Center. “Across the country, communities are grappling with how to preserve local access to advanced care. Our donors have sent a powerful message that they want top-tier healthcare available to the community, and they are willing to invest in making that vision a reality.”
The fundraising success advances Jupiter Medical Center’s $500 million Generational Health campaign, a long-term initiative supporting the organization’s strategic vision to expand service lines, deliver leading-edge specialty care, recruit nationally recognized physicians, invest in next-generation technology and develop facilities capable of serving a rapidly growing region. The campaign has currently raised more than $293 million toward its goal and is on track to end a full year ahead of schedule because of this year’s fundraising momentum.
“There was a time when patients in our community felt they needed to travel to the Northeast to access highly specialized care,” continued Rastogi, who has overseen the hospital’s transformation since 2019. “Instead, now we have patients heading south for high-quality care at Jupiter Medical Center. Times have changed, largely thanks to the unwavering support of our donors.”
Jupiter Medical Center is currently undergoing the most transformative period. The health system has significantly expanded its clinical capabilities and physical footprint by creating and growing the Anderson Family Cancer Institute, developing the comprehensive Robson Heart and Vascular Institute, opening the state-of-the-art Johnny and Terry Gray Surgical Institute, and adding the highly specialized 92-bed Tim and Jayne Donahue Patient Care Tower. Looking ahead, the medical center plans to open its second hospital in Avenir in early 2028 and will soon break ground on the Margaret W. Niedland Breast Center expansion to increase access to advanced imaging services. Together, these investments have transformed Jupiter Medical Center into a leading regional healthcare destination. This growth reflects the hospital’s continued evolution as a comprehensive health system with increasingly sophisticated clinical capabilities across a broad range of specialties.

articles.title: UC Davis spinout Delix Therapeutics raises USD 100m Series C after Phase Ib MDD data
articles.snippet: UC Davis spinout Delix Therapeutics raises USD 100m Series C after Phase Ib MDD data AllSci
articles.text:
Massachusetts-based Delix Therapeutics closed a USD 100 million Series C financing to take zalsupindole into Phase II. The company said a Phase Ib trial in adults with recurrent major depressive disorder (MDD) produced an approximately 50% mean reduction in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale scores at Day 8, maintained through Day 36. ​
Johnson & Johnson, through Johnson & Johnson Innovation – JJDC, Inc., and SV Health Investors' Dementia Discovery Fund led the round. Existing investors RA Capital, UC Investments, Artis Ventures, OMX Ventures, Dolby Family Ventures, and Bail Capital participated, as did new investors including Adage Capital Management, Hamilton Square Partners Management, Vestal Point Capital, and YK Bioventures. Christian Jung of SV Health Investors and a JJDC representative have joined the board. The company's previous financings include a USD 70 million Series A in September 2021 and a convertible note financing of more than USD 30 million in January 2022 .
Zalsupindole is an orally bioavailable neuroplastogen inspired by 5-MeO-DMT (mebufotenin). Delix says it is engineered to promote structural and functional neuroplasticity without hallucinatory, dissociative, sedative, or other psychotomimetic effects. The company reported no such effects across more than 120 participants studied to date. It expects to start a placebo-controlled Phase II proof-of-concept trial in recurrent MDD in the first half of 2027, with a trial design that includes at-home administration.
Proceeds will also fund additional development candidates and expansion of the company's neurodegeneration program, which the company says has shown preclinical efficacy signals. The platform traces to the lab of David E. Olson at the University of California, Davis , which identifies Delix as a spinout. David E. Olson co-founded the company.

XLIO Secures Additional $100 Million to Build Startups for Corporate Acquirers
News provided by
XLIO Ventures
10 Nov, 2026, 13:30 GMT
Share this article
Share this article
Global Made to Order™ startup builder to add Austin office, led by CEO Ron Kornfeld
AUSTIN, Texas , Nov. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- XLIO has secured an additional $100 million to make its total available funding facility $150 Million. The funds will be deployed to build Made to Order startups for leading technology companies. CEO Ron Kornfeld will lead its new Austin, Texas office.
Made to Order gives organizations a different route to access new technology. Rather than buying an existing company and adapting it, a client defines the exact capability it needs. XLIO then funds and builds a dedicated startup to deliver it, located and incorporated wherever best suits the client. Once the company hits agreed KPIs, usually within one to three years, the client acquires both team and technology. Deals typically range from $10 million to $50 million.
The new funding allows XLIO to run more Made to Order engagements in parallel and to extend the model into both new sectors and geographies.
The Austin office, at 801 Barton Springs Rd, Austin 78704, Texas, puts XLIO close to the engineering talent, founders and corporate buyers that Made to Order is designed for. Austin-based startups raised a record $7.19 billion in venture funding in 2025, up 64.8% on 2024, according to Crunchbase.
That startup economy in the region has deep roots. IBM, Texas Instruments and Motorola opened operations in Austin between 1967 and 1974, and Dell was founded in the city in 1984. Their early presence built the engineering talent base that later drew the headquarters of companies such as Tesla to the region and now feeds a new generation of startups.
"Austin's startup economy is vibrant," said Ron Kornfeld, CEO of XLIO Ventures. "There's deep engineering talent here, a steady stream of experienced founders, and a business community that backs new companies. I've moved here because I want our clients to share in that. Made to Order lets a business tap into Austin's talent and pace to get the exact technology it needs, built by a team focused on nothing else. This funding means we can help many more of them gain a foothold here."
About XLIO
Founded in 2020 and headquartered in London and Seattle, XLIO Ventures gives organizations a new route to acquire the technology they need. Through its Made to Order™ model, XLIO funds and builds a dedicated technology company around a single client's exact need, then transfers it to the client through acquisition only once agreed performance goals are met. Led by CEO Ron Kornfeld and backed by private equity, XLIO works with technology vendors and other large organizations that build advantage by investing in their own proprietary technology. Learn more at xl.io.
Media contact
Andrew Moloney, XLIO Ventures, press@xl.io

South African fintech Yoco secures $100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital Advisors
0
By
Tapiwa Matthew Mutisi
on
November 9, 2026
Africa , Fintech , Funding , Investments , SMEs , Startups
Yoco Technologies , the South African fintech company backed by global private equity firm TPG Inc., has secured a $100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital Advisors LLC (VPC), a U.S.-based alternative investment manager with approximately $3.6 billion in assets under management.
The funding represents a significant milestone for Yoco as it continues expanding its financial services ecosystem for small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) across South Africa.
Funding to Expand Merchant Financing
According to reports, Yoco plans to use the new credit facility to strengthen and expand financing opportunities available to its growing network of merchants.
The company has evolved beyond its origins as a point-of-sale (POS) payments provider and now offers a broader suite of digital commerce solutions designed to help small businesses accept payments, manage operations, and access working capital.
The $100 million facility will enable Yoco to extend additional funding to merchants that use its platform, helping business owners access capital needed to purchase inventory, invest in growth, manage cash flow, or navigate seasonal fluctuations.
Access to affordable financing remains one of the biggest challenges facing SMEs in South Africa, making merchant-lending solutions an increasingly important area of growth for fintech companies.
Yoco’s Evolution Into a Full-Service Fintech Platform
Founded in 2015, Yoco initially built its reputation by providing simple card payment devices and digital payment solutions to small businesses that were often underserved by traditional banks.
Over time, the company expanded its offering to include:
Payment acceptance solutions
Point-of-sale systems
Business management tools
Online payment services
Merchant cash advances and financing products
Digital commerce solutions
Today, Yoco serves hundreds of thousands of merchants across South Africa, ranging from informal traders and restaurants to retail stores and service-based businesses.
The company’s technology-driven approach enables it to analyse transaction histories and business performance data, allowing it to offer financing products tailored to merchants’ actual business activity rather than relying solely on traditional credit assessments.
Strategic Backing From TPG
Yoco has attracted significant investor interest in recent years, including backing from TPG Inc. , one of the world’s largest private equity and alternative asset management firms. The involvement of TPG has provided Yoco with additional capital and strategic support as it expands its footprint within South Africa’s rapidly growing digital payments market.
The latest facility from Victory Park Capital further strengthens Yoco’s ability to scale its lending operations without diluting existing shareholders, as debt financing allows the company to access growth capital while maintaining ownership structures.
Victory Park Capital’s Growing Fintech Portfolio
Victory Park Capital has become an active investor in financial technology and alternative lending businesses globally.
The firm specializes in providing flexible capital solutions to companies operating in sectors such as:
Financial services
Fintech
Consumer lending
Asset-backed finance
Small business financing

SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rox, which researches and develops the world's best revenue agent for the Global 2000, today announced a $100 million Series B financing at a $1.3 billion valuation.
The round is co-led by General Catalyst and March Capital, with existing investors Sequoia Capital and Factory doubling down on their investment, alongside new investors including Databricks Ventures and Prosperity7 Ventures.
In its first year in market, Rox has grown annual recurring revenue by more than 10x and is now deployed by leading public and private enterprises in non-tech industries including IT services, energy, commodities, medical technology, industrial manufacturing and automotive.
Rox is seeing more than 700% net revenue retention across enterprise customers, and some are seeing ~25x return on investment within 90 days.
The financing follows Rox's $50 million seed and Series A announced in November 2024. Zach Frankel, an early investor in Ramp, Cognition and Applied Compute, is also an early backer of Rox.
Built for the sellers who drive revenue
Enterprise sales follows a power law: the top 15% of reps bring in roughly 90% of revenue. However, the average rep spends 40% of their time on administrative work, according to Salesforce. Rox was built to raise the ceiling for those teams.
The Rox agent helps automate pipeline generation, deal execution, and upsells, so reps can better manage complex accounts and build relationships.

Rox is a vertically integrated, enterprise-ready AI system built on each customer's individual data warehouse. The results are already changing sales economics:
For a global IT services firm, Rox delivered $330M in qualified pipeline in eight weeks. Reps also handed off pursuit prep to Rox and got 1,000 hours back for selling.
For a global medical technology company, Rox has identified $200M+ of new funding opportunities at medical facilities that the team is actively pursuing. Despite multi-year sales cycles for some opportunities, Rox has already helped the team close $24M in revenue in just five months.
For a leading global engineering and professional services firm, Rox identified over $310M in potential opportunities, spanning signal-qualified leads and estimated net-new pipeline from previously missed public-sector bids.
For a market-leading DevSecOps platform, Rox doubled outbound volume. Rox has transformed them into an agent-driven org and delivered millions of dollars of pipeline.
For a leading payroll provider, Rox opens up an entirely new source of growth: autonomously finding and engaging 4M prospects the sales team couldn't economically reach, and turning them into meetings at just 20% of the cost of traditional outreach.
For a global industrial software company, Rox doubled sales team capacity and delivered 50+ meetings in just six weeks.
For a large German engineering and technology company, Rox delivered 24.3x ROI in 90 days by automating sales work the business had never been able to do before, from always-on pipeline tracking to personalized outreach at scale.

articles.text:
Rox Raises $100M at $1.3B Valuation as Aramco-Backed Prosperity7 Bets on AI Revenue Agents
Published on: 13 November، 2026
Rox
Rox, the AI startup developing autonomous agents for enterprise sales, has raised $100 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation,
Rox, the AI startup developing autonomous agents for enterprise sales, has raised $100 million in Series B funding at a $1.3 billion valuation, with participation from Prosperity7 Ventures, the venture capital arm of Saudi Aramco.
The round was co-led by General Catalyst and March Capital, with existing investors Sequoia Capital and Factory participating alongside new investors, including Databricks Ventures.
From Customer Data to AI-Powered Sales Execution
Rox develops AI revenue agents designed to help large enterprises identify commercial opportunities, generate sales pipelines and automate customer-facing workflows.
Its platform supports tasks ranging from prospect research and lead qualification to personalized outreach, meeting scheduling, deal management and account expansion.
The agents operate within companies’ existing systems and leverage enterprise customer data to support sales execution.
Rather than simply generating recommendations or content, Rox aims to enable AI agents to take action across revenue workflows and deliver measurable commercial outcomes.
ARR Grew More Than 10x in Its First Year
Rox said its annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew more than tenfold in its first year in the market, as the platform expanded across enterprise customers in technology, energy, industrial and financial services sectors.
Its customer base includes companies such as Groq, Ramp and Puma Energy. Rox also reported net revenue retention exceeding 700% among enterprise customers, reflecting significant expansion in revenue from existing accounts.
The company is positioning its platform around measurable business impact, including pipeline generation, customer engagement and sales productivity.
Funding to Accelerate AI Research and Enterprise Expansion
Rox plans to use the new capital to advance AI research, develop custom models and strengthen its evaluation infrastructure for real-world revenue tasks.
The company also intends to expand its enterprise customer base across healthcare, industrial manufacturing, financial services, energy and technology.
Why AI Revenue Agents Are Attracting Investors
The funding highlights a broader shift in enterprise AI, from tools that generate content or assist employees to agents capable of executing complex workflows and connecting data with business actions.
Sales is emerging as a major application area because it involves extensive customer data, repetitive administrative tasks and multiple interconnected processes, from prospecting to account management.
However, the long-term opportunity for Rox will depend on its ability to demonstrate sustainable customer returns, scale enterprise deployments and compete with established customer relationship management platforms.
The investment underscores growing venture capital interest in AI agents that can deliver measurable operational and commercial outcomes, positioning autonomous enterprise workflows as a major frontier in AI adoption.

articles.text:
Stage 2 Capital: $100 Million Fund Close Expands Early-Stage B2B AI Investing
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 5:02 PM
Stage 2 Capital: $100 Million Fund Close Expands Early-Stage B2B AI Investing
Stage 2 Capital has closed $100 million across Venture Fund IV and Catalyst IV, expanding its investment capacity for early-stage business-to-business AI companies while introducing an AI agent to help founders access its operator network.
Venture Fund IV will make investments of $2 million to $5 million in companies from seed through Series A. Catalyst IV will invest $200,000 in pre-seed businesses, often participating in their first institutional financing.
Both funds combine capital with support from experienced go-to-market executives. Stage 2 uses a pod model that pairs a venture investment partner with a partner whose background is in operating go-to-market functions.
The firm’s limited partner network includes more than 1,000 leaders with experience across sales, marketing, customer success, revenue operations, partnerships and forward-deployed engineering. Network members come from companies including Anthropic, OpenAI, Databricks, Lovable, SpaceX and ElevenLabs.
Stage 2’s new MCP agent is designed to connect portfolio founders with relevant expertise and relationships in that network. The firm says the agent will help identify operators who have recently addressed problems similar to those facing a portfolio company.
The system draws on the firm’s Science of Scaling framework, developed by Co-Founder and Managing Partner Mark Roberge. That framework helps companies assess when they are ready to scale and how quickly to grow.
The fund close follows four portfolio transactions: Salesforce’s acquisition of Momentum, Mainsail’s acquisition of Steelhead, Avalara’s acquisition of Versori and PSG’s majority investment in Order.co.
Stage 2 has already begun deploying the new funds, backing businesses including Letter.ai, Qualitate and Axle. The firm led Letter.ai’s $10.6 million Series A, which was followed four months later by a $40 million Series B led by Battery Ventures.
KEY QUOTES
“We started Stage 2 Capital because early-stage founders need more than capital. They need investors who can help them navigate their operational challenges. No firm solved this well for go-to-market.”
“That’s been true since day one, and these latest funds demonstrate the success of the model. We’ll always be in the room with our founders. Now, with AI, we can more easily surface the collective expertise, experience, and connections across our LP network, connecting founders with the right people and insights at the moment they need them”
Jay Po, Co-Founder And Managing Partner Of Stage 2 Capital
“We see founders make the same two mistakes over and over. Some scale too slowly and miss their window. Others scale before they’re ready and put the entire business at risk. We have well-established ways to measure revenue, but very little discipline around deciding when a company is actually ready to scale or how fast it should grow. Too often, boards rely on a playbook that worked for another company ten years ago, without considering whether it makes sense for the business in front of them. We want to help founders and investors make those decisions based on evidence rather than assumptions.”
Mark Roberge, Co-Founder And Managing Partner Of Stage 2 Capital

articles.title: Databento Raises $100 Million Series C at $1.1 Billion Valuation
articles.snippet: Databento Raises $100 Million Series C at $1.1 Billion Valuation PR Newswire
articles.text:
Databento Raises $100 Million Series C at $1.1 Billion Valuation
News provided by
Databento Inc.
Nov 12, 2026, 08:57 ET
Share this article
Share this article
SALT LAKE CITY , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Databento, the market data platform for modern finance, today announced a $100 million Series C financing at a $1.1 billion valuation. The round was led by Fifth Down Capital, an early investor in Databento, with participation from nearly all of the company's existing investors, including NEA, DRW Venture Capital, Tribe Capital, and Hedosophia.
The announcement follows Databento's $97 million Series B earlier this year. Since closing its previous round, the company has more than doubled its revenue while remaining profitable.
Databento serves leading quantitative trading firms, brokerages, asset managers, commodities firms, and digital asset companies. The company has also established a strong presence in artificial intelligence, having signed enterprise contracts with five of the six leading frontier AI labs.
Databento had 39 employees when it closed its Series C, reaching a $1.1 billion valuation with a fraction of the headcount of traditional market data providers.
"In this AI era, we're seeing remarkably small teams build billion-dollar companies, but that level of efficiency is unprecedented in the market data industry," said Christina Qi, co-founder and CEO of Databento. "Until now, reaching this milestone required hundreds of employees given the sheer scale of physical infrastructure involved. I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished, and we'll continue to prioritize exceptional talent as we grow."
"Fifth Down first invested in Databento pre-revenue, as we recognized early on that the company had an opportunity to challenge the established model for delivering financial market data," said Andrew Spellman, founder and CEO of Fifth Down Capital. "Our confidence has only grown as Databento's traction and execution have demonstrated it can serve demanding institutional customers, sustain rapid growth, and build a profitable business. Databento's performance has reinforced our original thesis and strengthened our conviction in the company. We are thankful to Christina and Luca for the opportunity to increase our investment and involvement by leading the Series C financing."
The round also included a strategic investment from Fitch Ventures, bringing the perspective of a leading financial information provider with deep expertise in credit ratings, financial data, and market insights.
"Financial data is becoming increasingly API-driven and machine-consumed, creating an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how institutions and other market participants access it," said Gabby Munoz, Global Head of M&A and Venture Investments at Fitch Group. "Databento has built differentiated infrastructure at the source and paired it with a modern, self-service model that makes institutional-grade market data available on demand. We're excited to back the team as they scale a platform we believe will help shape how market data is captured, delivered, and consumed."
The new funding will support Databento's continued investment in its market data infrastructure and expansion into additional asset classes.
